statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Roughly forty-five minutes into the US cash session the Nasdaq-100 is trading two-sided rather than directionally: NQ futures are 29,106.75, down 0.06%, inside a 28,927.50-29,170.00 range whose low has been fully retraced, while the cash index is 29,137.35, up 0.21%. VIX has fallen to 15.62, a fresh session low, and WTI is $89.61 after fading from $92.29. Tail eases to 16 because the observed path shows retracement remaining available rather than repeated extension.
recommendation: The observed structure is the opposite of the pathological case: a marginal session low that was retraced, an opening auction that neither gapped nor extended, and a volatility surface easing as crude retreats from its highs. Stress stays high at 65 because the drivers are structural rather than intraday - an active US-Iran exchange around the Strait of Hormuz, crude on an $89-90 handle and a 10-year yield that reached 4.814%, its highest since November 2023. Tail remains well below the block threshold. The single identified mechanism for index-level one-way structure in the next 24 hours is scheduled: Broadcom, a top-five constituent, reports after the 20:00 UTC close with its management call at 21:00 UTC, and the 22:00 UTC futures reopen must price that in one move. The danger window is therefore set narrowly at 20:00-23:00 UTC. Existing-position management and emergency protection are described as remaining active throughout.
headline: Nasdaq-100 retraces its session low as VIX slips to 15.62 and crude fades from $92: Tail eases to 16, with the Broadcom close the only projected block-band window
body:
The US cash session has now been open for roughly three quarters of an hour and has not produced the continuation structure that earlier cycles treated as the main near-term risk. NQ futures trade 29,106.75, down 18.75 points or 0.06%, inside a day range of 28,927.50 to 29,170.00. The cash Nasdaq-100 is 29,137.35, up 0.21% against Tuesday's 29,077.22 close, in a 28,971.90 to 29,138.15 range. S&P 500 futures are 7,668.50, up 0.34%, and the broader tape is firmer still, with the Dow up around 0.70% and the Russell 2000 up around 0.92%. The session low has been fully retraced and price sits in the upper half of the range. A marginal low that holds, followed by a rotation higher rather than a one-way extension, is the direct opposite of the repeated-extension-after-failed-retracement path that defines mean-reversion failure, and it is the primary reason Tail steps from 17 to 16.

Cross-asset evidence points the same way. VIX is 15.62, down 0.72 or 4.41% from its 16.34 close, and is printing at a fresh session low of 15.59 after reaching 16.82 earlier. Crude is retreating rather than extending: WTI is $89.61, down 0.68%, having marked $92.29 during the episode. The August ADP report printed 38,000 private jobs against a 47,000 consensus, the slowest pace since January, and July factory orders came in at +0.9% against a +0.6% consensus. Volatility, crude and the equity tape are therefore de-escalating together rather than aligning into a single amplified impulse, which is the configuration in which Tail normally stays low even while Stress remains high.

Stress eases only marginally, from 66 to 65, and stays in the high band because its drivers are unresolved rather than repaired. US forces have continued striking IRGC targets around the Strait of Hormuz, with explosions reported on Qeshm Island and at Bandar Abbas, Chabahar, Jask and Sirik; two supertankers carrying Saudi oil were struck while transiting outbound earlier in the week, and Iran's parliament speaker has publicly linked its own export capacity to that of the wider Gulf. Against that backdrop the 10-year Treasury yield reached 4.814%, its highest since November 2023, with sovereign yields climbing in parallel in the UK, Germany, France and Japan. The shared Finviz cross-asset context was collected at 00:35 UTC and is far beyond the 90-minute freshness bound, so under the inherited contract it is treated as stale and this assessment rests entirely on independently fetched primary sources. Confidence is 88 on directly observed index, futures, volatility and crude quotes, two verified macro prints and a confirmed calendar.

The dominant forward risk is scheduled rather than current. Broadcom reports fiscal Q3 results after the 20:00 UTC cash close, with the management call at 21:00 UTC, alongside Snowflake and Hewlett Packard Enterprise. Broadcom's June 2026 report produced a 12.6% single-session decline despite beating on revenue and earnings, driven by forward AI revenue commentary on the call rather than the printed quarter, with guided Q3 AI semiconductor revenue near $16.0 billion the stated reference point. A repricing of that magnitude in a top-five constituent, landing in a thin post-close book and then compressed into the 22:00 UTC futures reopen after the 21:00-22:00 UTC CME maintenance halt, is a credible mechanism for index-level one-way structure with a delayed second leg. That is why the projection lifts Tail above the block threshold for exactly two hours - 26 at 20:00 UTC and a peak of 27 at 22:00 UTC - and why the danger window is placed narrowly at 20:00 to 23:00 UTC rather than across the session. Before then, the EIA crude report at 14:30 UTC and the Beige Book at 18:00 UTC are treated as checkpoints, neither lifting projected Tail out of the low band. Mapped policy state: EA_ON.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-one of the 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment; the 15:00 and 20:00 UTC hours on 1 September and the 01:00 UTC hour on 2 September have none and are marked unavailable. The window opens in the aftermath of the Hormuz escalation, with Tail oscillating between 21 and 25 through the 1 September US afternoon in event/whipsaw mode and a single orange print of 25 at 19:00 UTC as Stress peaked at 77. Through the overnight hours Tail held a narrow 20-23 band while Stress stayed between 71 and 75, reflecting an absorbed retaliation wave rather than a trending one. Mode shifted to trend-down from 09:00 to 11:00 UTC during the European morning, with Tail between 20 and 23, before the 12:00 UTC hour marked the clear break: Tail fell to 18 and Stress to 68 as ADP printed soft and crude began retreating from its highs, returning the reading to the EA_ON band and mixed mode for the first time in more than 24 hours. The 13:00 UTC hour extended that at Tail 17 and Stress 66 as the cash open printed orderly. The sequence describes a regime that escalated sharply, held elevated for roughly a day, and has decayed steadily since the European morning without ever reaching the strong-block region.
outlookSummary: The projection keeps Tail inside the low band for the remainder of the US cash session, ranging between 16 and 19, with the 18:00 UTC Beige Book the only scheduled lift and no hour resting on assumed directional structure. It then crosses the block threshold for exactly two hours around the after-close earnings block: 26 at 20:00 UTC, when Broadcom, Snowflake and Hewlett Packard Enterprise report into a thin post-close futures book, and a peak of 27 at 22:00 UTC, when futures reopen after the 21:00-22:00 UTC CME maintenance halt and must price the results and the 21:00 UTC Broadcom management call in a single move. The intervening 21:00 UTC hour is held at 24 because the futures book is halted for most of it. That two-hour cluster is the basis for the 20:00-23:00 UTC danger window, and it rests on a named scheduled catalyst with a documented 12.6% single-session precedent rather than on any observed price structure. From 23:00 UTC the projection decays through 23, 21 and 20 as Asian liquidity rebuilds, reaching a projected overnight trough of 18 between 04:00 and 06:00 UTC - held above a normal quiet-night level because the Hormuz escalation remains unresolved in thin books. It lifts to 19 across the European session, then to 20 for the 11:30 UTC Challenger release and 22 for the Thursday data block containing Initial Jobless Claims and the trade balance at 12:30 UTC and the cash open, S&P Global Services PMI and ISM Services from 13:30 UTC. Confidence decays with horizon from 88 to 57, reflecting that the current reading rests on directly observed price-path evidence while later hours rest on conditional scenarios.
